value.overview: The Golden-fronted Woodpecker (Melanerpes aurifrons) is a woodpecker recorded in the United States. Field recognition often comes from golden nape, barred back, pale head, sturdy bill, and bold black-and-white wing pattern. In the U.S. source data, it appeared in 2 state or DC summaries, including OK, TX. It is most associated with Forests:  Tropical Dry, and local season should be checked before trip planning.
value.classification: The Golden-fronted Woodpecker belongs to the family Woodpeckers in the order Piciformes. This is the practical birding classification used for the BirdIntel profile cache.
value.identification: Look for golden nape, barred back, pale head, sturdy bill, and bold black-and-white wing pattern. Also use size, posture, flight style, voice, behavior, habitat, and season. Plumage can vary by sex, age, molt, and light, so the safest identification comes from combining several field marks rather than relying on one color or feature.

Cavities are important for nesting success, and both adults may help with excavation, incubation, and feeding young. Mature or structurally diverse Forests:  Tropical Dry is often valuable.
value.dietFeeding: It eats insects and other arthropods taken from bark, branches, trunks, and sometimes the ground. It may also take fruit, seeds, or sap depending on season. Foraging usually involves climbing, probing, tapping, or flaking bark.
value.behavior: It climbs trunks and branches using stiff tail feathers for support. Calls, drumming, and repeated visits to favored trees are often useful clues. Many woodpeckers defend territories during the breeding season.
